country.evidence_quote: urban populations [United States, n = 44 ( Human Microbiome Project Consortium, 2012 ; Lloyd-Price et al., 2017 )]
country.notes: Brazil/Venezuela stated directly ('inhabit the Amazon region encompassing the Brazil and Venezuela border'). Peru inferred from 'Matses from the Peruvian Amazon'. Tunapuco only described by region 'Andean highlands' without explicit country.

body_site.section: Materials and Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
body_site.notes: Applies uniformly to all groups analyzed (gut microbiome/stool samples).

days_from_first_collection.notes: Single stool sample collected per subject; no longitudinal collection reported.

lifestyle.evidence_quote: two hunter–gatherer communities [Yanomami from Venezuela, n = 8 ( Clemente et al., 2015 ); Matses, n = 24
lifestyle.notes: Tunapuco described as 'a rural agricultural community [Tunapuco, n = 12 ( Obregon-Tito et al., 2015 )]'. US group not assigned a traditional lifestyle category in the text.

probing_pocket_depth.notes: Not applicable; study concerns gut microbiome, not periodontal measurements.

westernized.evidence_quote: compared taxonomically and functionally with the Yanomami from Venezuela...and an urban-industrialized group
westernized.notes: Traditional groups (Yanomami/Brazil, Yanomami/Venezuela, Matses, Tunapuco) contrasted with the 'urban-industrialized group' (US).

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: The datasets generated for this study can be found in the NCBI under the BioProject PRJNA527208
ncbi_accession.notes: Accession refers to newly generated Yanomami/Brazil metagenomic data; other groups' data are from previously published external studies without accessions given in this text.

age.notes: Age data mentioned as collected but not reported in main text ('age and gender information of the individuals were also acquired... summarized in Supplementary Table 1').

ancestry.notes: No explicit ancestry category reported; only ethnic/cultural group names (Yanomami, Matses, Tunapuco) given.

sex.notes: Gender collected and analyzed for association with microbiome composition (PERMANOVA test comparing female/male Yanomami/Brazil) but individual sex values not reported in text.

zigosity.notes: Not applicable; no twin study design reported.

dietary_restriction.notes: General dietary description given (low in fat/salt, high in fruits/fiber/sylvatic animals) but not a formal dietary restriction category.

disease.evidence_quote: Common chronic diseases in modern societies, as atherosclerosis and obesity are virtually unknown among Yanomami
disease.notes: Statement is a general population-level claim (citing Mueller et al., 2018), not a direct clinical assessment of the study participants; treated as inferred/low-confidence health status.

disease_details.evidence_quote: Common chronic diseases in modern societies, as atherosclerosis and obesity are virtually unknown among Yanomami
disease_details.notes: No formal disease diagnosis reported; inferred healthy status from statement that common chronic diseases are absent among Yanomami participants.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable/not mentioned in this microbiome study.

pmid.notes: PMID not stated within the provided text body.

target_condition.notes: The study focuses on gut microbiome diversity/function in traditional vs urban groups rather than a specific disease phenotype; no explicit target condition/phenotype is stated as the study focus.
